description: Verify that TCP in TIME-WAIT acknowledges a retransmitted FIN and restarts the 2*MSL time-out (RFC 793 §3.9 p73)
approach:
[Objective]
A peer's retransmitted FIN reaching DUT in TIME-WAIT signals that DUT's earlier ACK was lost. RFC 793 §3.9 requires DUT to ACK the replay and reset the 2*MSL clock — otherwise the binding could close while the peer is still trying.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Handshake → CLOSE → FW1 → tester ACK + FIN → DUT in TIME-WAIT.
2. Tester → DUT: replay FIN.
3. Observation: DUT → Tester: ACK.
4. Wait 1.5*MSL (less than full 2*MSL).
5. Tester → DUT: second replay FIN.
6. Observation: DUT → Tester: ACK (still in TIME-WAIT, clock restarted).

[Pass condition]
Both replay FINs get ACK.

[Fail condition]
Any prelude or replay-ACK missing.

verdicts.Pass: DUT acked replay FIN and restarted 2*MSL — normal
verdicts.Fail_no_tester_fin_ack: No DUT ACK to tester FIN
verdicts.Fail_no_first_replay_ack: No DUT ACK to first replay FIN in TIME-WAIT
verdicts.Fail_no_second_replay_ack: No DUT ACK to second replay FIN after 1.5*MSL
